_note: THE THREE DIFFICULTY SETTINGS. Global, chosen on the level select screen, remembered in the save, and fixed for the length of a level once it has started. Every number the game reads is here; nothing about difficulty is hardcoded.
_whatTheyChange:
SEVEN KNOBS, AND THE LIST IS STILL DELIBERATE. It was two -- starting lives and starting peanuts -- and the reasoning that kept it at two is reproduced below because most of it is still correct and the part that is not is the part that changed.
STILL TRUE, AND THE REASON THERE IS NO ARMOUR, DAMAGE OR SPEED SCALAR. Scaling armour would change WHICH TOWERS ARE VIABLE rather than how hard a level is: the Grinder ignores armour and the Slingshot cuts it, so a difficulty that raised armour 30% would not make the level 30% harder -- it would make one tower better and another nearly useless, and the draft would decide the run before the player did. The same objection covers enemy damage and enemy speed against the towers whose whole value is their fire rate. Those three are not here and must not be added.
NO LONGER TRUE OF LAZY DAD MODE: 'it would force every level to be tuned three times'. The 35-45% band is a statement about `normal` and only about `normal`. Lazy Dad Mode does not have a band to hold -- it has one requirement, that a young child gets through -- so it is soaked once to confirm where it lands and then left. There is no third set of tuning to maintain, because there is no third target.
THE HEALTH SCALAR IS THE ONLY ONE THAT TOUCHES THE ACTUAL PROBLEM, and it is admitted rather than hidden. Two of the ten levels fail on a boss DPS check -- level 2's Devil at wave 13 and level 10's Vlaude -- and on those a player reaches the boss with every pad filled and money spare, so extra lives and a fatter purse change nothing at all. Measured: see reports/2026-09-16-lazy-dad-mode.md. Lowering health without lowering armour does make armour-piercing towers relatively better, exactly as the armour objection says; at the shipped 0.7 it is swamped by the effect and it is the price of the mode working.
_normalIsANoOp: `normal` MULTIPLIES BY 1 ON EVERY KNOB AND MUST CONTINUE TO. Every soak number in SOAK-REPORT.md, every per-level win rate and the whole 35-45% target band were measured against rules.json's shipped values, and they stay valid only while the default difficulty changes nothing at all. tests/difficulty.test.ts asserts it against rules.json directly rather than against a copy, so a change to either file that breaks the identity fails the build. EVERY KNOB ADDED HERE MUST DEFAULT TO 1.0 FOR BOTH `normal` AND `try-hard` -- try-hard's published behaviour is lives and purse only, and it was not re-soaked for anything else. `Difficulty.ts` returns the input UNTOUCHED when a multiplier is exactly 1, so the no-op is exact rather than a rounding that happens to land on the same integer today.
_ordering: The list order is the order the selector draws them in, easiest first. The selector reads this array; it does not carry its own list.

modes.name: Lazy Dad Mode
modes.blurb: Three times the lives, longer between waves, and everything on the board hits softer. Built for small hands.

modes.name: Yeah, I Game
modes.blurb: The game as it was tuned. Every published win rate is this one.

modes.name: Try Hard
modes.blurb: Half the lives, a thin purse, and the same enemies. Leaks are what kill you.

_rounding: Lives ROUND and floor at 1; peanuts ROUND and floor at 0. A difficulty that could hand out zero lives would end the run on the first leak before the player had done anything, which is not a difficulty setting, it is a broken level. The floor is in Difficulty.ts so both the game and the soak get the same number from the same function.
_healthRounding: Enemy health ROUNDS and floors at 1, and a def with no health at all stays at 0. The floor is what stops a future 0.1 from rounding a 1-health enemy to 0 and putting something on the board that is dead on the frame it spawns. The 0 case is left alone because `EnemyDef.maxHealth` is nullable so an unfinished level's boss can exist as data before its number does, and turning that into a 1 would hide it.
_startingPeanutsFloor: THE PURSE FLOOR IS NOT HERE and must not be. `Economy.openingPurse` already guarantees the opening purse covers the cheapest tower this run actually drew -- that is what `startingPeanutsMargin` is for -- and it is applied AFTER the multiplier. So Try Hard's 0.75 makes the opening slower without ever making the first instruction in the game impossible to follow, and a second floor here would fight the one that already works.
